feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant public-sector impact. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo shows increasing scope, responsibility, and credibility.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms make achievements believable.  
- Strong alignment between headline, competencies, experience, and technical skills; the profile is coherent and market-relevant.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears often across summary, competencies, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections like Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scale metrics: include % improvements, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings, or adoption outcomes where possible.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”. No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it is slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground public-sector scale and leadership impact.
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger action-led phrasing such as “leading modernization of” or “shaping.”
- Trim the long capability list to the most differentiating strengths; let skills sections carry the rest.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds and scales enterprise digital platforms, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader”; consider varying one of them.
- The list of analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled experiences repeats content covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items into fewer, sharper categories; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial systems & content operations • Analytics, reporting & optimization • AI-enabled search, automation & platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, livestreaming & event delivery
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “content operations” or “digital communications leadership” for stronger specificity and less generic phrasing.
- Consider “AI-enabled search and content experiences” → “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences” to better match the projects/work history.
- Keep style parallel across all items; most are noun phrases, so avoid mixing broad functions with channel-specific outputs.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several phrases from the header almost verbatim: “enterprise web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled user experiences.”
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills; if both sections remain, this block should stay higher-level while Topline Skills handles detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and context.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Built/Developed/Launched…” and trim stacked descriptors.
- Clarify unique value in each item, especially audience/business purpose, not just features.
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently; spell out “10 x 20-foot” for cleaner formatting.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search overlaps with the current freelance role bullet on “AI-enabled search initiative.”
- Advocacy Video Series and parts of the Anniversary Campaign overlap with NACo video/studio and multimedia accomplishments in Work Experience.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and make the scope/results more concrete.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type + remit in one line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by streamlining CMS workflows, front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and cross-team publishing processes.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experience.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift, search success, or publishing efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo prior NACo roles, so emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with transformation, infrastructure, and team/operating model impact.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-channel operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific or measurable: add email open/click growth, audience growth, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten this bullet.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving executive reporting and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and efficiency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-program language may duplicate earlier NACo roles unless this bullet stresses the studio build and expanded in-house capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned before stepping into broader strategy/governance leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show build-out: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable or operational outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/planning language; keep this item focused on execution and channel management.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this as scaling/operationalizing the series, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated terms tied to current positioning:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & information design
- Use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more current, executive tone.
- Swap “messaging” for “communications” or “content operations” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space is tight, cut to 4 bullets by removing “Audience-focused content planning,” since that idea is implied elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats language already established in the summary and work experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work: Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations/automation, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent/relevant tools first; move lower-signal items like WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages later or remove if not central to target roles.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based workflow systems” for clarity and stronger business relevance.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Drupal platform delivery” or “enterprise CMS modernization” signals scale better than just product names.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section carry the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; retain it here only if this is a target differentiator.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be more specific about level/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same skills section.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Platforms:** Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put the most relevant/recent platform first and signal depth: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content)** if space allows.
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just Power Pages.
- If you want stronger impact, replace GitHub Pages with a more business-relevant platform only if used materially in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is largely duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or using one section for platforms and the other for implementation skills.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent experience, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **JavaScript • HTML5/CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery**
- Consider adding light context if format allows: **JavaScript/HTML/CSS for CMS theming and front-end implementation • API integrations • GTM • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers unless required; **HTML/CSS/JavaScript** is cleaner than **HTML5/CSS3**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- If **workflow automation** stays in Topline Skills, don’t also imply it here via GitHub Actions unless you frame this item specifically as technical tooling.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is useful but currently reads as a mixed tool dump rather than a focused skills line. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so it should emphasize systems actually central to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Split automation tools from collaboration/project tools to improve clarity and signal depth.
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”; move Slack, Teams, and Basecamp later or remove.
- Consider renaming to: “Automation, Workflow & Project Systems” if keeping Jira/Asana/Trello/Slack/Teams.
- Tighter rewrite: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello” or, if broader coverage is needed, “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project systems: Jira, Asana, Trello.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis without adding specificity.
- Slack and Teams are generic workplace tools and add little differentiation unless central to your workflow leadership.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/strength via modifiers rather than outcomes already covered elsewhere, e.g. **enterprise email automation**, **member communications**, **newsletter operations**
- Optional rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email automation, member engagement, newsletter operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience entries.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language; it’s already covered in Core Competencies and multiple roles.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to emphasize methods and reporting capability rather than repeating exact tools already highlighted in recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as grouped capabilities: “Web analytics & reporting: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Replace vague nouns with stronger skill phrasing: change “Dashboarding” to “dashboard development” or “executive KPI reporting”
- Clarify optimization methods: “SEO analysis • A/B testing • conversion/performance optimization”
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first based on recent roles: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity …”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one version or making this one tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the Director role, so avoid overloading this section with identical phrasing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early digital operations, and concrete outputs from this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add specific outputs if available: website refresh size/traffic impact, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or production volume.
- Tighten the leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving cross-channel workflows across web, email, social, and video. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating website modernization language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; produced digital and multimedia content to extend member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast line stronger and more concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience/downloads, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.
- Consider separating research/program support from digital production so the item reads as two clear contributions rather than a list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on the podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads like a mixed list of software and capabilities and overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize concrete tools and keep broader production capabilities elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Audio/Video Tools**
- Replace with a cleaner, tool-first list: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
- If you want to retain capability signals, make them more specific: **Livestream production workflows • Podcast recording/editing**
